statement:
Implement `validate_build(schemas, root, operations)` for a binary-record builder containing schema-backed records and homogeneous arrays.

A descriptor is:
- `"int"` or `"text"`;
- `("record", s)` for schema index `s`;
- `("array", d, c)` for elements of descriptor `d` and capacity `c`.

`schemas[s]` is a tuple of layout terms:
- `("field", name, d)` contributes one field;
- `("repeat", t, r)` contributes the complete flattened layout of earlier schema `t`, repeated `r` times.

Flattening is recursive and order-preserving. Each schema references only smaller schema indices and has at least one flattened field. Flattened layouts may be enormous.

The builder starts with one open `("record", root)`. Each operation affects the most recently opened, unclosed container:
- `("put", name, p)`, where `p` is `"int"` or `"text"`, inserts one value;
- `("open", name, d)`, where `d` is a record or array descriptor, inserts that value and opens it;
- `("default", k)` inserts default values into the next `k` positions without opening containers;
- `("close",)` closes the current container.

For an ordinary insertion into a record, an unfilled field must remain, and its name and descriptor must exactly match the next flattened field. For insertion into an array, `name` must be `None`, unused capacity must remain, and the descriptor must equal the declared element descriptor. Descriptor equality is recursive and includes schema indices and capacities.

`default` is valid in a record only when at least `k` fields remain and every one of those fields has descriptor `"int"` or `"text"`; it fills them in schema order regardless of their names. In an array, it is valid only when the element descriptor is primitive and at least `k` capacity slots remain. The entire operation is invalid if any requested position is invalid.

An array may be closed at any length. A record may be closed only when all flattened fields are filled. Closing the initial record leaves no current container, making every later operation invalid.

Return the 1-based index of the earliest invalid operation. Return `0` if all operations are valid and the initial record is closed by the final operation. If all operations are valid but any container remains open, return `len(operations) + 1`.

Constraints:
- At most `200_000` schemas and operations.
- At most `300_000` total layout terms and descriptor nodes.
- Names have length at most 40.
- Repetitions, capacities, and default counts are between `1` and `10^18`.
- Schema-reference and descriptor nesting are at most 60.
- All arguments have the stated tuple forms and valid indices.

Use only the Python standard library and perform no I/O.
